question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I began with the assigned guide, tried a specific C# style discovery query, then a broader style query when the first returned no matches. The broader match was unrelated, so I listed vocabularies and found csharp.style-choices and csharp.style-tiers. I requested both HAL resources before inspecting either response, expecting choices and tier descriptions to be separate. The choices response actually embedded all tier descriptions, choice values, complete Boolean property sets, and conflict groups, so it contained enough to answer. I then followed its describedby contract link to check how omission and map coverage were represented; that read did not supply a fact needed for the final answer. My first jq filters assumed the generic envelope shape and then lost the root scope; I corrected them to retain data_scope, map coverage, sets, groups, and embedded tier values. After that filtered view, I stopped product requests because the requested facts were present and complete. The separate tier and contract requests were unnecessary in hindsight.
